title: Show reviewers the value of a text block

blocks.text: Twice this quarter a text block passed review and then produced the wrong string in production: once a padded record that came out short, once a message whose every line had gained four spaces. A diff can't show either. The team's review bot will now post, under every text block a pull request changes, the exact string the compiler makes of it.

`TextBlockPreview.value(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/TextBlockPreview.java` receives the block's source lines exactly as they are in the file: everything after the opening delimiter's line, up to and including the line with the closing `"""`. It already splits off the closing delimiter and joins the lines. Finish the two `TODO`s:

items: `margin(...)`: how many leading characters javac removes from every line of the block;
`strip(...)`: what is left of one source line in the value.

blocks.text: When you're done, `value(...)` returns exactly the string javac produces for any block of spaces, tabs and text, without escape sequences. About eight lines in total.
The tests compare with values that javac 21 produced from the same lines.

cases.says: a block whose closing delimiter is aligned with its content loses its common indentation and keeps the nesting inside it
a block whose closing delimiter follows its last line gets the same treatment and no final line break
empty and whitespace-only lines leave the removed indentation unchanged and come out empty
a closing delimiter on its own line, left of the content, leaves the difference in front of every line
a closing delimiter on its own line, right of the content, removes no more than the content allows
whitespace at the end of a source line is not part of the value
a tab counts as one character of indentation, like a space, not as several columns

origin.section: A Tab and a Space Each Count as One Character

concepts: Blank lines, empty or whitespace only, take no part in the count and come out empty, so the value does not depend on how an editor treats them.
A closing delimiter on its own line left of the content leaves the difference in front of every line.
A closing delimiter on its own line right of the content removes no more than the content allows.
javac removes from every line of a text block the smallest leading-whitespace count among its non-blank lines and the closing delimiter's line; indentation beyond it is kept.
A tab counts as one character of indentation, like a space, so a tab-indented line among space-indented ones comes out misaligned.
Whitespace at the end of every line of a text block is removed, so padding typed in the source is lost.
